_README: Podcast episodes picked for a hike (#1683 - Offer podcast episodes picked
for the hike, with a one-tap Spotify save and an in-app player).
THIS FILE IS EDITORIAL. Every row is somebody's call that an episode is
worth hearing on a particular hike, and a diff of this file reviews those
calls. Nothing searches Spotify for episodes and nothing ranks them.
ONE ROW PER EPISODE:
spotify_id  the 22 characters after /episode/ in its open.spotify.com link
title       the episode's title, as Spotify prints it
show        the show's name, as Spotify prints it
minutes     its length in whole minutes, or leave it out - absent prints
no length, never a guessed one
hikes       suggested-hike ids it belongs on (the hike detail screen),
e.g. nynjtc_hike_finder:7909
at_miles    A.T. mile ranges it belongs on, as [start, end] pairs counted
from Springer (the Today screen, when the day a hiker planned
overlaps a range). Typed by hand from a guidebook, so loose by
a mile or two against the app's own axis - which is fine for a
podcast and would not be for anything a hiker's safety rests on
pois        published POI ids the episode talks about (#1718 - Tag podcast
episodes to the places they talk about), e.g. atc_shelters:<uuid>.
The episode shows last on each of those places' cards, under
"Listen here"
places      the same POIs' names, in the same order, so a diff can be read
without looking ids up. Checked against reference/
poi_identity.json: a POI never published or since retired, or a
name that is not the ledger's, costs the row
links       optional: the episode's link in the other podcast apps a hiker can
pick (#1690), each one copied from that app's own Share / Copy
Link: {"apple_podcasts": "https://podcasts.apple.com/...",
"pocket_casts": "https://pca.st/...", "overcast":
"https://overcast.fm/+...", "youtube_music":
"https://music.youtube.com/..."}. An app left out sends that
app's listeners to Spotify with a line saying it is not linked yet
reviewed    the date somebody last looked at this row (YYYY-MM-DD)
note        optional: why it fits. Kept here for review, never published
A row needs at least one of `hikes`, `at_miles` or `pois`, or it shows nowhere.
tests/test_export_podcasts.py fails on any row export_podcasts.py would drop,
so a typo here is a red pull request rather than an episode that silently
never appears.
WHERE THE PLACES COME FROM: the Podcast desk, a private claude.ai page
(features/PODCASTS.md). Claude proposes the places an episode's notes and
transcript mention and shows the words it matched; a person decides. The
places on one episode are at least 500 trail miles apart (the maintainer,
2026-09-29). The desk enforces that with export_poi.py's miles; nothing
here can, because this file holds no miles (lib/podcasts.py says why), so
a hand edit keeps the rule on its honour.
THE GREEN TUNNEL ROWS (48 of the show's 51 episodes, 2026-09-29): places
proposed on the desk by Claude Code, pushed by the maintainer as one list
("push the list"). Titles are the show's feed's, which a Spotify search
matched to each id. A note beginning "Mentioned in passing" is a place the
episode names without spending time on it, given to an episode that had no
other place and only where that place had no other episode; "Added at the
maintainer's request" is a place the episode does not name. The three left
out are two trailers that name no place and "Music of the Mountains", whose
places are all off the trail.
THE NATIONAL PARK AFTER DARK ROWS (21 of the show's 469 episodes,
2026-09-29): the show's own episode map (npad.bounds.earth, read from its
sheet) pins each episode to a park, not to the spot the story happened. An
episode is a candidate when its pin is within 15 miles of the A.T. or its
notes name a park the trail crosses. A place the notes name is matched to
its ATC POI; otherwise the park gets one spot, the same for every episode
set there ("One spot for the whole park" in the note, the maintainer's
rule, 2026-09-29). Crime stories are tagged where they happened. Classified
by Claude Code by those rules and committed at the maintainer's word
("when done, commit here"), not ticked place by place on the desk; the
note on each row says what the match rests on. Episodes about other trails
and parks wait on the desk. OurHike publishes places off the A.T. (nearby_poi,
places.json), but lib/podcasts.py accepts only ids in reference/
poi_identity.json, the A.T.'s ledger (#1721).
GRANDMA GATEWOOD (2026-09-29): National Park After Dark's episode about her
and The Memory Palace's "Emma and the Trail" share three places chosen from
her history at the maintainer's request ("Grandma gatewood is a must! find
some places meaningful for her"): where the trail she walked begins, the
museum that keeps her shoes, and the summit where she finished. Neither
episode's notes name a place, so each note says "Added at the maintainer's
request". The trail in Ohio named for her waits on the desk: it is off the
A.T., and under 500 miles from two of the three.
PUBLISHING: .github/workflows/publish-podcasts.yml, dispatched by hand. It
writes podcasts/episodes.json at the bucket root, outside any release
folder, so a phone sees a new list on its next fetch with no app release
(maintainer's decision, 2026-09-26, on #1683).

episodes.title: Founding the Trail
episodes.note: Katahdin Summit (W): Myron Avery's Katahdin, which became the northern terminus largely to his credit, and Baxter State Park's rules today.

episodes.title: What Came Before
episodes.note: Rausch Gap Shelter: Rausch Gap, Pennsylvania, the coal-mining and railroad town the trail passes through; named 12 times in the transcript. Bluff Mountain (the lost boy, 1891) is left off: it is 383 miles away, inside the 500-mile rule.

episodes.title: Iconic Locations: McAfee Knob
episodes.note: McAfee Knob Summit: The whole episode, including the nine years the trail was routed off the Knob.

episodes.title: Changemakers
episodes.note: Blackburn Trail Center Group Campsite: The Blackburn Trail Center is named for Ruth and Fred Blackburn; Sandi Marra's first volunteer job was managing it.

episodes.title: Iconic Locations: The Lemon Squeezer
episodes.note: Island Pond: The Lemon Squeezer is on the A.T. in Harriman at about mile 1391 (OpenStreetMap puts it 0.1 mi from ATC's mile-1391 marker). ATC's list has no point named for it; Island Pond, 0.4 mi away, is the nearest.

episodes.title: Danger!
episodes.note: Washington Monument Vista: The two sisters struck by lightning while sheltering inside Maryland's Washington Monument.

episodes.title: Trail Food
places: Pine Grove Furnace State Park Parking Area 1
episodes.note: Pine Grove Furnace State Park Parking Area 1: The camp store's Half Gallon Challenge, begun in 1980 near the halfway point. Maupin Field Shelter is left off: 262 miles away.

episodes.title: Iconic Locations: Maryland's Washington Monument
episodes.note: Washington Monument Vista: The whole episode.

episodes.title: Leave Only Footprints
episodes.note: Max Patch Mtn Summit Vista: The 2020 overcrowding and trash on Max Patch; named 24 times in the transcript. | Katahdin Summit (W): Baxter State Park's rules for hikers finishing on Katahdin.

episodes.title: Iconic Locations: Mount Washington
episodes.note: Mt Washington Summit Vista: The whole episode.

episodes.title: Give Me Shelter
episodes.note: Tumbling Run Shelter 1: The Tumbling Run Shelters' snoring and non-snoring pair, maintained by Curt and Tawnya Finney since 1989. | Kinsman Notch (NH Rte 112) Parking Area: Serena Ryan's Notch Hostel in North Woodstock, New Hampshire. The hostel is not an ATC point; Kinsman Notch, on NH 112 toward town, is the nearest trail point.

episodes.title: Iconic Locations: Oglethorpe Monument
episodes.note: Springer Mtn Summit Vista: Where the southern terminus moved from Mount Oglethorpe. Oglethorpe itself is off today's trail, so it is not among ATC's points.

episodes.title: Helloooo!
episodes.note: Katahdin Summit (W): Eiler Larsen began the first recorded thru-hike attempt on Katahdin in August 1930.

episodes.title: Hiking McAfee Knob with Virginia Outdoor Adventures
episodes.note: McAfee Knob Summit: The whole episode; named 17 times in the transcript. Tinker Cliffs and the trailhead are within a few miles, so they are left off.

episodes.title: Craving Community
episodes.note: Hot Springs: The Smoky Mountain Diner and its owner, Genia Peterson. | Delaware Water Gap: Susan Cooper's Village Farmer and Bakery, run for 45 years. | Monson: Shaw's Hiker Hostel and Monson as an official Trail Town; named 13 times. Roan Mountain (Bob's Dairyland) is left off: 138 miles from Hot Springs.

episodes.title: Gear Up
places: Walasi Yi Center (Neels Gap, US 19 & US 129) Parking Area
Pine Grove Furnace State Park Parking Area 1
episodes.note: Walasi Yi Center (Neels Gap, US 19 & US 129) Parking Area: Mountain Crossings at Neels Gap, the outfitter known for pack shakedowns. Added at the maintainer's request; the episode does not name it. | Pine Grove Furnace State Park Parking Area 1: The Appalachian Trail Museum at Pine Grove Furnace, whose gear collection the episode visits: Grandma Gatewood's shoes and old packs.

episodes.title: Iconic Locations: Mount Greylock
places: Mt Greylock Summit Observation Tower Vista
episodes.note: Mt Greylock Summit Observation Tower Vista: The summit and its lighthouse-shaped memorial tower.

episodes.title: Uprooted
episodes.note: SHEN - Skyland South Parking Area: Skyland, named 7 times, beside the hollows whose families were removed for the park. Nicholson Hollow, the episode's main community, is not an ATC point.

episodes.title: Iconic Locations: Monson, Maine
episodes.note: Monson: The whole episode.

episodes.title: Crappalachian Trail
episodes.note: Roan High Knob Shelter: The host's 2019 visit after the bubble passed: the highest shelter on the trail, in the one state with no privies at shelters. | Little Rock Pond Shelter: Where the first moldering privy was built, in 1997.

episodes.title: Iconic Locations: Roller Coaster
episodes.note: Ashby Gap (VA Rte 601) Parking Area: The Roller Coaster runs 13 miles from Ashby Gap to Snickers Gap; one end is enough under the 500-mile rule.

episodes.title: Native Persistence
places: Clingmans Dome Summit Lookout Tower Vista
episodes.note: Clingmans Dome Summit Lookout Tower Vista: The episode opens on settler names like Clingmans Dome replacing Indigenous ones; the Cherokee are reclaiming its name, Kuwahi. The episode's main place, the Monacan Nation's Bear Mountain, is not on the A.T.

episodes.title: Iconic Locations: Damascus, Virginia
episodes.note: Damascus: The whole episode.

episodes.title: The Lost AT
episodes.note: Damascus: The southern end of the lost 300-mile section, which ran from Damascus to McAfee Knob by a different route. McAfee Knob is left off: 244 miles away.

episodes.title: Finding Virginia's Lost AT with Dakota Jackson and Mills Kelly
episodes.note: Damascus: The same lost section as "The Lost AT", which ran from Damascus to McAfee Knob.

episodes.title: Iconic Locations: Center Point Knob
episodes.note: Center Point Knob Vista: The whole episode.

episodes.title: The Call of the Trail
episodes.note: Bears Den Rocks: Where a guest's section hike south from Bears Den led to the conversation that changed her life. | Katahdin Summit (W): The same guest's finish on Katahdin after 207 days.

episodes.title: Iconic Locations: Harpers Ferry
episodes.note: Bolivar/Harpers Ferry: The whole episode: John Brown's raid and the landscape hikers pass through.

episodes.title: The Weight of History
episodes.note: Tray Mtn Shelter: A 1981 threat against Black hikers written in the shelter register, which the episode discusses. | Bolivar/Harpers Ferry: Where the host found the story in ATC's archives, and a guest walks into town thinking about its history.

episodes.title: Iconic Locations: Fontana Dam
episodes.note: Fontana Dam: The whole episode: the dam and the towns under Fontana Lake.
Damascus: Added at the maintainer's request; the episode does not name Damascus.

episodes.title: A Life Crafted for the Outdoors with Orange Blaze
episodes.note: Springer Mtn Summit Vista: The A.T.'s southern terminus, the end nearest Florida. Added at the maintainer's request; the episode is about the Florida Trail, not the A.T.

episodes.title: Hiking Connecticut with "Jester" Section Hiker
episodes.note: Bear Mtn Summit (CT) Vista: Bear Mountain in Connecticut, after Sage's Ravine; named 11 times.

episodes.title: Season Three: The Natural History of the Trail
episodes.note: West Kennebec River: Mentioned in passing: the trailer names the Kennebec River Ferry as one of season three's iconic locations. ATC lists both banks; the west bank, where a northbound hiker waits for the canoe, is a guess between them. The Priest, the trailer's other place, already has an episode.

episodes.title: Geological Time
episodes.note: Massie Gap Vista: The Grayson Highlands, whose rocks come from ancient volcanoes near Mount Rogers and Whitetop. | Clarendon Gorge: A geologist's favorite place on the trail, near Clarendon, Vermont.

episodes.title: Iconic Locations: Dragon's Tooth
episodes.note: Dragons Tooth Peak: The whole episode.

episodes.title: The Perfect Tree
episodes.note: Manassas Gap Shelter: Mentioned in passing: the host maintains this shelter, one of the first the CCC built, from chestnut logs cut on the mountain nearby and still sound almost 90 years on.

episodes.title: Iconic Locations: Charlies Bunion
episodes.note: Charlies Bunion Vista: The whole episode.

episodes.title: Constructing the Trail
episodes.note: Blood Mtn Shelter: The stone shelter a CCC crew built on Blood Mountain. | SHEN - Skyland South Parking Area: Shenandoah, where CCC crews built the stone huts and moved the trail around Skyline Drive; a 1930s hike to Skyland lodge. | Sugarloaf Summit (NE): The last two miles of the trail, finished by the CCC between Spaulding and Sugarloaf on August 14, 1937.

episodes.title: Iconic Locations: Bear Mountain Bridge
episodes.note: Bear Mountain Bridge: The whole episode.

episodes.title: Wayfinding
episodes.note: Poplar Ridge Lean-to Shelter: The 1969 Maine guidebook's turn-by-turn passage the episode reads, past the Poplar Ridge Lean-to toward Saddleback Junior.

episodes.title: Iconic Locations: Delaware Water Gap
episodes.note: Delaware Water Gap: The whole episode.

episodes.title: Becoming a National Park
episodes.note: Springer Mtn Summit Vista: The 1957 move of the southern terminus to Springer Mountain, as development closed in on the last 37 miles. | Boiling Springs: The Cumberland ("Carlisle") Valley, where land for the trail's cornfield miles was taken in court. Boiling Springs is the valley's trail town; the episode names the valley, not the town.

episodes.title: Iconic Locations: Priest Mountain Shelter
episodes.note: The Priest Shelter: The whole episode: the confessions in the shelter's logbook.

episodes.title: Trail Writing
episodes.note: Pearisburg: Mentioned in passing: Mary Draper Ingles followed the New River home after her 1755 escape, as a novel retells it. The A.T. crosses the New River beside Pearisburg; ATC's list has no point for the bridge, so the town stands in. Hot Springs, the episode's other trail place, already has an episode.

episodes.title: Iconic Locations: The Katahdin Sign
episodes.note: Katahdin Summit (W): The whole episode: the sign on the summit. ATC lists two summit points; this one is a guess between them.

episodes.title: Hogs, Chipmunks, and Bears, Oh My!
episodes.note: Newfound Gap Vista: The feral hogs of the Smokies. The episode names the park, not a point; Newfound Gap stands in for it. | Front Royal/Warren County: The Smithsonian's research center at the north tip of Shenandoah, which the trail runs through.

episodes.title: The End of the Trail
episodes.note: Cornelius Creek Shelter: The host's own green-tunnel moment, just north of Cornelius Creek Shelter. | Saddleback Summit: David Field's favorite stretch of the whole trail: the Saddleback alpine ridge.

episodes.title: Unsolved: Shenandoah and Acadia National Park
episodes.note: SHEN - Skyland South Parking Area: One spot for the whole park (the maintainer, 2026-09-29): the notes place the story in Shenandoah National Park but at no named point on the trail. This park's spot is Skyland, the A.T.'s stop at the park's lodge. The show's map pins Acadia, the episode's other half, which is off the A.T.

episodes.title: Cannibals? Great Smoky Mountains National Park
episodes.note: Newfound Gap Vista: One spot for the whole park (the maintainer, 2026-09-29): the notes place the story in Great Smoky Mountains National Park but at no named point on the trail. This park's spot is Newfound Gap, where the A.T. crosses the park's main road.

episodes.title: Lore and Lingering Spirits: Haunted National Park Trails
episodes.note: Newfound Gap Vista: One spot for the whole park (the maintainer, 2026-09-29): the notes place the story in Great Smoky Mountains National Park but at no named point on the trail. This park's spot is Newfound Gap, where the A.T. crosses the park's main road. The park is one of five in the episode.

episodes.title: Three Points of No Return: Bermuda Triangles of North America

This park's spot is Glastenbury Mountain, the peak the forest's run of disappearances is known by (the "Bennington Triangle"); that name is reasoned, not in the notes. The forest is one of three places in the episode.
